column2: Put the ark on the last row that says IMAGE READ
column5: *** DONE, 14 September 2026 - the fifth ark is found, and the act came with three other things. *** *** EMA SIXTA LERENA JUANICO's marriage act: ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-T7P2-W *** - "La Union, Montevideo, Montevideo. Religious Marriage Records 1902-1934", act 90 of 30 June 1913, FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ. *** THE ROUTE THIS ERRAND PRESCRIBED WAS WRONG AND A SIMPLER ONE WORKED. *** It said to browse the La Union register by DGS through the catalogue. In fact the register is IN FULL TEXT, and a phrase search for *** "Sixta Lerena" *** returns exactly two documents, the first of which is it. Two earlier rounds failed because they searched her with MASSERA as spouse and searched Jose Pedro Massera by name; the compound SIXTA LERENA had not been tried. *** WHAT THE ACT SAYS: *** "Don Jose Pedro Mar[s]era, natural de esta Republica, soltero, de cuarenta y seis anos de edad, hijo legitimo de Don Jose Joaquin Mar[s]era y Dona Mercedes Martinez, finados = con = Dona Ema Sixta Lerena Joanico, de la misma nacionalidad y estado, de treinta y tres anos de edad, *** hija legitima de Don LUIS LERENA LENGUAS y Dona JULIA JOANICO, FINADOS *** . Fueron testigos, Don Jaime Herrera y Dona Maria Perena Juanico de Herrera." *** THREE THINGS BEYOND THE ARK. *** *** (1) Her parentage is now on an ACT, not an index *** - Luis Lerena Lenguas and Julia Juanico named as her parents in her own marriage. *** (2) BOTH PARENTS WERE DEAD BY JUNE 1913 *** - "finados" - which this archive did not have. *** (3) It corrected her sister's surname in this register: *** the witness "Maria PERENA JUANICO de Herrera" is Maria Lerena JUANICO, and the register had her as LERENA LENGUAS, her father's compound rather than her own. *** The age of 33 on the act is NOT adopted: *** this archive already settled her birth at 21 November 1876 on three independent records, and ages at marriage are the weakest date in genealogy.

The 1895 Buenos Aires census enters a JOSEFA in Gilberto Lerena's household as *** "LERENA de L[erena], m, 43, VIUDA, R. Oriental" *** - and on the two lines above her the same enumerator writes married women as [maiden surname] de L. If he is consistent, Josefa was born a Lerena and married a Lerena, one generation before Juan Carlos. *** BUT WITHIN THE HOUR, Uruguayan civil registration produced a JOSEFA LERENA married to FERNANDO MORATORIO, whom the FamilySearch tree attaches to Josefa Lerena Traibel 1851-1947 - the same candidate. If that is her, "de L." is the enumerator's shorthand for the Lerena HOUSEHOLD and proves nothing. The Lerena-Lerena reading is withdrawn as evidence. *** She is almost certainly the Josefa Lerena who stood godmother at the Catedral de Montevideo in 1885. Born about 1852, widowed by 1895. Look for her marriage in Montevideo 1870-1890, and for her husband's death before 1895. And note the dispensation sweep that concluded no Lerena-Lerena marriage exists is itself known to be blind to compound surnames.

column2: Find the GRANADA marriage act of Sancho Lerena y Armenta and Ana Maria de Aguilar
column5: *** DONE, 14 September 2026 - the act was found, and then the reason for wanting it was withdrawn. *** *** FamilySearch ark 1:1:C9WG-BGW2 indexes it: SANCHO DE LERENA Y ARMENTA, born CORDOBA, son of SANCHO DE LERENA Y VELASCO and MARIA ANTONIA DE ARMENTA Y GUEBARA, married ANA MARIA DE AGUILAR of La Malaha, daughter of FRANCISCO DE AGUILAR and BEATRIS FRANCO, at SANTA ANA, GRANADA on 17 NOVEMBER 1754. *** A second index entry sits in the Granada Pre-Marriage Investigation Files (ark 1:1:XPG2-RYP). *** BOTH ARE MARKED IMAGE UNAVAILABLE - the act itself is still unread, and Geneanet's fifty-year span is now a single day. *** *** BUT IT DOES NOT TOUCH THIS FAMILY. *** The errand existed because a son of that couple would be styled Lerena y Aguilar, which is the name the trees give the Uruguayan Sancho. *** The jfina tree gives his parents as FELIX LERENA and ROSALIA AGUILAR, citing Revista 15 IEGU - so Aguilar is his MOTHER'S surname, not a Granada grandmother's. *** *** And full text agrees from the other side: "Juan de Lerena y Aguilar" returns FIVE Madrid notarial hits, "Sancho de Lerena y Aguilar" returns No Results Found against that control. *** The Spanish findings are kept as Spanish findings in data/1754-granada-act.tsv, under a banner withdrawing the connection.

column2: *** Revista 15 IEGU, pages 53-54 - no longer the only authority, but still worth having ***
column5: *** DOWNGRADED 15 September 2026, and the reason is good news. *** This errand was headed "the ONLY authority for Sancho's parents", because the Geneanet pages of FELIX LERENA and ROSALIA AGUILAR carry nothing but the line "Family: Revista 15 IEGU" and this archive had used that parentage to withdraw the Granada hypothesis. *** THE PARENTAGE IS NOW ON A PARISH ACT. *** The baptism of their grandson Luis Escolastico at the Iglesia Matriz of Montevideo, 10 February 1811, reads "Abuelos paternos FELIZ GERENA y ROSALIA AGUILAR" - ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-X7F6-M. *** So the article is no longer load-bearing and nothing in this archive now depends on it. *** *** IT IS STILL WORTH GETTING, for a different reason: *** the act gives the parents' NAMES and nothing else. Felix and Rosalia have no dates, no places, no marriage and no other children anywhere here. *** If Revista 15 cites a Spanish act for them - a parish, a book, a folio - that is the first thread into CORDOBA, which is still on no act at all. *** *** If it cites nothing, the article can be set aside for good. *** Same place as before: the IEGU sells back issues (www.iegu.org.uy, plain http - its certificate has expired); also at Stanford (SearchWorks 458344) and HathiTrust (record 101485627).

column2: *** Apolant, "Operativo Patagonia", ficha 355 - the source of the 1791 date ***
column5: *** The 8 January 1791 date, carried here for days as "what the trees say", descends from a named published work with a numbered entry. *** JUAN ALEJANDRO APOLANT, "Operativo Patagonia: historia de la mayor aportacion demografica masiva a la Banda Oriental, con la nomina completa, filiaciones y destino de las familias pobladoras" (Montevideo, Imprenta Letras, 1970), *** FICHA 355 *** - the FERNANDEZ TRESGUERRAS family, Asturian colonists of the 1778-1781 convoy. *** NOT AVAILABLE ONLINE: *** archive.org does not hold it; HathiTrust holds it (catalog record 008709228) but serves a bot check and, as a 1970 imprint, would be search-only. Second-hand copies appear on MercadoLibre Argentina. *** WHAT TO LOOK FOR: what APOLANT himself cites for the marriage *** - he worked from the parish books and the AGN, so his footnote may name the very book and folio this archive has been hunting. *** And whether he gives the PLACE, which the tree does not. ***

column2: *** gendatabase.com - the one record worth paying for ***

This archive had never tried it. *** Free summary rows already gave death years for all three sons of the 1950 estate. *** The full records are behind a subscription, and this session does not create accounts or pay for things - so this is yours to decide. *** *** IF YOU BUY ONE THING, BUY THE DEATH NOTICE OF RICARDO JUAN CARLOS LERENA, born 1920, died 1994, married 1941 to Doreen May Chappell. *** A South African death notice names *** the deceased's PARENTS *** - which would put in a modern official document what this archive currently infers: that the Cape Lerenas descend from Pablo Armando. *** Second priority: the five 1999 deaths *** - Catherine Tertia Karon, Gayle, Pierre Frederick, and two children aged 8 and 13. column2: Run one GRO index search: TAYLOR births, mother's maiden name BRAYLEY, Bideford, 1870-1890
column5: *** THIS IS THE SEARCH THAT ENDS THE TENTH-CHILD QUESTION, and it cannot be run from here. *** *** gro.gov.uk is NOT FreeBMD ***, and the difference is the whole point: the GRO's own online index *** gives the MOTHER'S MAIDEN NAME on every birth from 1837 ***, which FreeBMD does not and never will. *** THE QUERY: births, surname TAYLOR, mother's maiden name BRAYLEY, district BIDEFORD, 1870-1890. *** By definition that returns *** every child of William Taylor and Mary Ann Hellen Brayley ***, with no inference, the missing tenth included. *** WHY IT IS DAVID'S: *** it needs a free GRO account, and this session does not create accounts or sign in. *** WHAT IS ALREADY EXCLUDED, so the result can be read fast: *** the baptism register at Northam holds seven children of this couple and nothing between 31 August 1881 and 30 October 1884 - so the child being looked for is one who left a birth registration and nothing else. *** EDITH (Sep q 1882) and ETHEL (Dec q 1882) are the two names in the Bideford birth index that sit in that window ***; neither is in the register. *** RUN AND ANSWERED THE SAME DAY: David logged this session in and the search was made. *** Nine children, all at Bideford, nothing missing - and the tenth child this archive had been hunting for three weeks does not exist. See /corrections/ and data/gro-taylor-brayley-births.tsv.

column2: *** Open the Montevideo death act of PEDRO A. LERENA, 6 November 1896, certificate 353 ***
column5: DONE THE SAME EVENING IT WAS RAISED, 12 October 2026, and the act confirms the index. Acta No. 353, 15a Seccion de la Capital, image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2W-H39V-V, PLATE READ at apid TH-909-72188-82458-0. PEDRO LERENA, nacido en Montevideo, 69 years old, casado, died at five in the afternoon of 6 November 1896 at calle Rivera No. 163 of tisis pulmonar, certified by Dr Vitale, before Vicente Carricaonde. 'HIJO LEGITIMO DE DON PEDRO A. LERENA, ORIENTAL, FALLECIDO, Y DE DONA VICENTA DE LA VEGA, ORIENTAL, FALLECIDA.' Wife: Dona Manuela, oriental, 53. Children named: ANTONIO, CARLOS TEODORO and MANUEL ANTONIO, plus the first declarant Don Pedro A. Lerena, soltero, empleado, 'hijo del fallecido'. WHAT IT SETTLES: which Pedro married Manuela Lemos, asked on this register's own row on 11 October. WHAT IT BREAKS: the date of household 229 - 69 in 1896 means born about 1827, and a man born 1827 is six in 1833, not sixteen. Either the census is later than c.1833 or the sixteen-year-old is a different son of the same couple. NEW ERRAND RAISED: re-date household 229.

column2: *** Date the enumeration behind household 229 - the volume says 1850, this archive says c.1833 ***
column5: SETTLED 12 October 2026 at CATALOGUE level. FamilySearch catalogue koha:1408224, 'Uruguay, Montevideo, censos, 1726-1860', lists film 7499042 item by item: item 1 = Padrones de habitantes, LIBRO 263, 1843; ITEM 2 = LIBRO 264, 1850; item 3 = libro 257, 1852-1853. Household 229 is in item 2, so the enumeration is the PADRON OF 1850. The c.1833 is withdrawn. CONSEQUENCES: the three derived birth years moved seventeen years later (Emilia c.1832, Pedro c.1834, Vicenta c.1838), and the head - entered at forty, so born about 1810 - IS NOT Pedro Antonio Lerena born 31 July 1793. That holds under the neighbouring 1843 book too, where he would be born about 1803. The c.1833 was itself inferred from the identification it was then used to support, which is why it stood. See data/corrections.tsv.

column2: Find LEONARDA MARGARITA LERENA VEGA after 1837 - she is not in the 1850 padron
column5: ANSWERED THE SAME EVENING, 12 October 2026. She was never missing from the padron of 1850 - only from her parents' house. She is entered at CASA 229 OF CALLE SARANDI (index ark 1:1:XMKF-FR3W, image ark 3:1:3QS7-89ZP-B99S-Z, plate read at apid TH-1961-36718-27970-97), blanca and oriental, aged ELEVEN where thirteen would be right. AND THE NUMBER WAS A TRAP: her parents are at a DIFFERENT casa 229 on another street, so there are at least two houses numbered 229 in one padron and 'household 229' was never an identifier. SHE IS ALSO THE ONLY WHITE PERSON IN THAT HOUSE: Estanislada 20 (morena), Sinforiano 19, Manuela 60 (patria AFRICA, casada) and Rosa 46 (oriental, casada) all carry the surname by ditto. Four people entered in their own right. See data/sarandi-229-1850.tsv.

column2: *** Read the Cordon burial register 1839-1852 for Estanislada, Sinforiano, Manuela and Rosa ***
column5: *** DONE 17 October 2026, AND THE FOUR ARE NOT IN THE BOOKS IT COULD REACH. *** All thirteen death and burial PAGES that full text returns for the surname are now opened - the other eleven today, six of them at the plate - and Estanislada, Sinforiano, Manuela of Africa and Rosa are in none. THAT IS A LIMIT ON THE INSTRUMENT, NOT A NULL ON THE BOOKS: each of the thirteen is the page where full text saw the surname, and a name written without LERENA is not on the list. What they gave instead is on /uruguay/ and in data/cordon-deaths.tsv: seven new people (Jose Maria Larranaga and his parents Benito and Martina Lerena; Sara Lerena and her mother Teresa; Jose Maria Reyes and Maria Lerena), the burial of Servando Gonzalez, husband of Estefania Lerena of San Jose and Trinidad, CONFIRMED the same day by his civil death act (no. 194, 25 May 1892), the widow Teresa Leonar de Lerena of 1901, CONFIRMED as Teresa Leonard by her civil death act (no. 252, 27 August 1901), and a husband, Carlos Alberto Fein, dead twenty-seven years before the 1946 registration that named him. WHAT WOULD STILL REACH THE FOUR: the Cordon death book itself, read page by page for 1839-1852, and the 1843 padron (libro 263), which is not indexed. THE ORIGINAL ERRAND, AS WRITTEN: The four adults who carry the LERENA surname at casa 229 of Calle Sarandi in the padron of 1850 - Estanislada 20, Sinforiano 19, Manuela 60 (patria AFRICA) and Rosa 46 - are recorded by a census that has NO COLUMN FOR CONDITION. A parish act would have one: burials and baptisms of this period write 'liberta', 'esclava de' or 'parda libre' outright. Nuestra Senora del Carmen La Mayor, Cordon - Religious Death Records 1839-1852 and Religious Burial Records 1885-1892 onward - are already identified in this archive's hands and unread, and the Catedral registers cover the same years. ALSO WORTH IT FOR ITS OWN SAKE: Manuela and Rosa are both recorded CASADA, so each has a husband who is not in that house. NARROWED 12 October 2026: the holder formula has been swept and it is NOT the route. 'esclava/esclavo/liberta de [holder]' was run as a phrase against every Lerena this archive can name. TWO POSITIVES, both already held: 'esclava de Don Sancho Lerena' returns the Montevideo Catedral act of 1812 (Juana and Maria Mercedes), and 'esclava de Don Alejandro Lerena' returns the San Jose baptism and burial of April 1846 (Barbara and Carmelo Anselmo). NOTHING for Pedro Antonio, Pedro, or Luis Lerena, and nothing for the male or 'liberta' forms. Two controls passed in the same session, so those are real nulls. WHAT SURVIVES: their acts may use 'parda libre' or 'morena libre', or name no holder at all - which is exactly how Barbara appears on the BURIAL even though her baptism names hers. SO IT MUST BE READ BY EYE. NOTE THE ABBREVIATION TRAP: 'D.n' matches nothing in full text; write 'Don' or drop the honorific. STARTED 13 October 2026. THE LIST EXISTS NOW: thirteen of the parish's ~95 Lerena documents sit in its death and burial books - Religious Death Records 1839-1852 and 1869-1877; Religious Burial Records 1885-1892, 1892-1897, 1897-1901, 1908-1914, 1918-1926. TWO READ, ELEVEN UNREAD. The four of Sarandi 229 are NOT in the two read. AND THE FORENAME ROUTE IS DEAD: 'Estanislada' with a Cordon place filter returns nine pages, about nine hundred documents, so neither the compound surname nor the forename is a handle - the eleven remaining documents must be read by eye. WHAT THE FIRST TWO GAVE INSTEAD: the deaths of Vicenta and Manuela Lavina, four and three, on 5 August 1869, 'hija de D. Xavier (hijo) y de la finada LEONARDA LERENA'; and an Amelia Lerena, nine, dead 11 November 1871.

column2: *** Sweep the South African Gazette on the SPELLINGS, not just LERENA ***
column5: The consul test of 12 October found no LERENA in any South African gazette before 1951, with both controls passing (coverage 1910-2026; 'exequatur' returns 644 documents with hits in 1914, 1932, 1933, 1937). THAT NULL IS ON ONE SPELLING. This archive's own rule says a null on one spelling is a null on a letter - and 1910s-40s gazette OCR is exactly where a surname breaks. RUN: SERENA, LLERENA, LORENA, LARENA, LEVENA, LERINA, GERENA, PERENA against gazettes.africa, filtering results on the /akn/za link prefix because the site's country= parameter DOES NOT BIND. Look only for pre-1951 hits. Search terms that find the right notices: 'Recognition granted as Consul-General', 'Recognition granted as Vice-Consul', 'exequatur'. *** DONE 17 OCTOBER 2026: NINE SPELLINGS, NO LERENA-LIKE SURNAME IN ANY SOUTH AFRICAN GAZETTE 1905-1950. *** Control reproduced (LERENA earliest April 1951). Detail on /consul/ or the consul-gazette test; the null is stronger and still an indication, not an answer.

column2: *** Look for Nuno Fernando Lerena's war service (Air Force, Western Desert) ***
column5: A 1997 letter from Gavin Knott says Nuno 'joined the Air Force and served in the Western Desert' after two years at school in Stellenbosch; he was 18 in 1942. A recollection - and a July 1971 'Deaths' notice signed '12th Squadron, S.A.A.F. Friend' now supports the Air Force; neither gives a service record, and the letter also misplaces his marriage. Test: SA Defence Force WWII nominal roll and personal files (Department of Defence Archives, Pretoria), with Nuno Fernando LERENA b. 6 Oct 1924 and service number unknown; and ask whether a 12 Squadron S.A.A.F. association or roll names him. UNIT SIDE, SEARCHED 16 OCTOBER 2026: the UK National Archives catalogue lists 16 items described as No 12 Squadron in series AIR 54 (South Africa Air Force: Operations Record Books). Those that could cover Nuno (18 from 6 October 1942): AIR 54/51/2 (1942), 54/52/1 (1942), 54/52/2 (1943), 54/53/1 and 54/53/2 (1943), 54/54/1 (Jan-Sept 1944), 54/185/5 (Oct-Dec 1944) and 54/191/2 (Jan-May 1945), inside pieces AIR 54/51, 52, 53, 54, 185 and 191 - all marked digitised, so downloadable. NOT YET OPENED: each piece is a large scan (a forum member put them near 250 MB), and David said to download the 1943 and 1944 pieces. They name aircrew in sortie reports far more than ground crew, so a miss would not disprove service. An absence from the Documentation Centre's roll would not disprove it either. DOWNLOADED AND MACHINE-READ, 16 OCTOBER 2026: David's order 3689478 brought down AIR 54/52, 53, 54 and 185 (2,892 images, 2.1 GB, kept outside the repository, private research only), and macOS text recognition found NO 'Lerena' in any form; the near-misses were checked on the page images ('A/Sgt Levin' and similar). That does not show he was not in 12 Squadron: the pieces hold crew lists far more than nominal rolls, ground crew are seldom named, and recognition on these scans is good but not a reading. His file at the Documentation Centre remains the test.
